theses.title: The one-paragraph story
theses.text:
## The one-paragraph story

A predecessor system (not present in this repo) proved the concept and then
collapsed under its own success: roughly 140 accumulated feedback rules loaded
as prose pushed fresh sessions toward 400–500k tokens of always-on context,
where rules fired wrongly or vanished when needed most. In the project's RPG
vocabulary, it brought the **whole stash into every map** — as if a character
carried gear for every damage type when the encounter called only for cold
resistance. In plain language, irrelevant rules consumed attention and created
unintended interactions before the task began. The author's implementation
answers with _compiled_ rules: each correction becomes a typed mechanism (a
permission, a guard, a reactor, an evaluator, a transformer, a workflow gate)
attached only where relevant. A session in that profile gets **a build, not a
biography** — one active behavior, a handful of linked supports, its selected
safety layer, and the exact task state. The platform supplies the compiler and
mechanism contracts without prescribing that loadout. The [starter proof](../evidence/WO-118/README.md) completed resident-owned scratch delivery and review repair with writer replacement and resident restart; a fresh export demonstrated live status, while efficiency remains unmeasured.

theses.title: The core bet
theses.text:
## The core bet

> "The true work of the inventor consists in choosing among these combinations
> so as to eliminate the useless ones... the rules that must guide the choice
> are extremely fine and delicate. It's almost impossible to state them
> precisely; they must be felt rather than formulated." — Poincaré, via Pirsig

Generation is cheap and getting cheaper; the scarce asset is the **selection
function** — the operator's sense of what is good, currently exercised one
correction at a time. DotLn's bet is not that this delicate judgment can be
exhaustively formulated. It is that useful operational approximations can be
progressively arrived at: source incidents preserve what was felt, candidate
mechanisms approach it from different directions, and regression fixtures show
where each construction agrees or diverges. As mathematical or geometric
techniques can converge on a shape without becoming the shape itself, the
formulation is an instrument for approaching the operator's selection function,
not a claim to contain it precisely. **The model changes; the organization
survives.** Claude, Codex, a human, a shell script, and a future model are
interchangeable occupants of the same actor slot.

That bet needs an excellent foundation before it needs a long feature list. In
the reference implementation, the smallest useful loop—declare intent, see what
the system understood, observe authorized progress, receive timely feedback,
and inspect evidence—should already feel responsive, legible, and worth
repeating. Competitive gap-filling does not excuse a weak loop. When another
system introduces a useful idea, DotLn first asks whether the exact behavior can
be accommodated by existing primitives, compositions, ports, and runtime
lowerings. If not, the difference becomes evidence for one missing primitive or
boundary, not permission to bolt on an opaque special case. Integration and
semantic accommodation are preferred to imitation; both preserve every
capability contract the receiving implementation declares and expose any
omitted or lossy capability.

theses.title: The differentiated interface
theses.text:
## The differentiated interface

DotLn's second thesis is about _authoring_, not running:

> "I will take the entire Business, Leadership, and Personal Development shelf
> at Barnes & Noble and just map them to different agent / subagent
> communication structures... at once anyone who has read those books is an
> expert in some feature of the app — and it turns all those books into
> programming books overnight."

The analogies are not documentation — **the analogies are the ways you mix and
match the agents**. Every pattern (5S, the Ladder of Leadership, mitigated
speech, Theory of Constraints, commedia dell'arte roles, the
Algorithms-to-Live-By policies) compiles into exact mechanics, and the same
compiled program renders through an open-ended set of isomorphically equivalent
views: an RPG character with a Path-of-Exile-style socket-and-link build, a
business pattern card, a statechart, a function table, a marble/Morse temporal
track, a TypeScript DSL, an event timeline. Friendly metaphors are authoring
languages, never camouflage: every view either provably compiles to the same
normalized program or is labeled a lossy projection with the exact mechanics one
click away.

### Shape-first synthesis

The operator uses situations and analogies to communicate a desired **shape**: a
relationship, interaction, transition, contrast, feedback loop, or felt quality.
Literal similarity to the reference is not the acceptance test unless a specific
literal detail becomes load-bearing. Preserve the experience first, then
progressively lower it through observable interaction, domain mechanics,
contracts and evidence, and finally technology selected from representative
environment evidence. An imperfect analogy can carry a precise requirement;
source accidents do not become ontology by resemblance.

This is the standing interpretation rule for earlier and future operator
ideation. Its fullest product expression is the first-party application thesis,
[`προτείνω`](11-protino.md), but it applies to the whole platform.

theses.title: Three horizons, one kernel
theses.text:
## Three horizons, one kernel

1. **Work operating system** — workstreams, disposable workers, evidence-backed
   completion, offline-capable state, a near-empty main thread. The immediate
   product.
2. **Executable pattern workshop** — the shelf-to-mechanism compiler and the
   drag-a-card-onto-an-agent authoring surface. The differentiated product.
3. **Agent ecology & simulation laboratory** — paired counterfactual runs,
   first-divergence detection, agent swaps, reflection-policy experiments over
   recorded event logs. The research product.

Horizon 3 must emerge from the same kernel (deterministic replay is what makes
counterfactuals possible at all) and is not allowed to distort Horizon 1.
The [workstream application candidate](12-workstream-application.md) develops
Horizon 1 through concrete end-user journeys and gradual workflow replacement,
including one outcome spanning multiple repositories. It leaves deployment and
application identity open and does not allocate another release rung.
[`προτείνω`](11-protino.md) is the operator-named application destination that
joins Horizons 2 and 3: prose-authored patterns and ad hoc interventions become
playable inside an inspectable counterfactual community. Naming the destination
does not move it ahead of the release ladder or make its application-local
content kernel doctrine.

theses.title: Mission — increase the chance of operator flow
theses.text:
## Mission — increase the chance of operator flow

This is the mission of the author's personal implementation and a motivating
use of the platform, not a compulsory objective or operating policy for every
DotLn owner.

AI-assisted work commonly falls into a babysitting mode: the operator repeatedly
restates context, supplies procedural guidance, coordinates tools and workers,
checks unsupported completion claims, recovers stalled work, and spends active
attention on the machinery instead of the idea. The desired alternative is not
unbounded improvisation or confidence without evidence. It is a sustained
creative flow in which the operator can keep the idea and implementation
direction in mind while the surrounding work behaves dependably.

The reference implementation's mission is to improve the conditions for that
**operator flow state**.
Supporting research, capability-building, coordination, routine procedure,
recovery, and verification should happen automatically when authorized,
predictably when routine, and helpfully when a genuinely material decision needs
the operator. Product and research investment should favor capabilities that
remove recurring supervision and avoidable context switches without exporting
their cost into correctness, authority, evidence, privacy, or recoverability.

The implementation cannot promise or infer a person's psychological state. It can
reduce interruption, repetition, manual ceremony, and rediscovery; preserve
intent and working context across handoffs; package necessary interruptions as
decision-ready inputs; and make recovery unsurprising. Under its selected
profile, flow does not silently authorize scope expansion, skipped verification,
perpetual action, or self-certification. “Give an agent a build, not your
biography” remains useful architectural shorthand for one mechanism serving
this larger mission.

exclusions.text:
Not an agent, an agent harness, or an agent-orchestration layer, as its
  identity. DotLn is an **agentic platform**: the shared substrate on which
  people and software actors hold work, authority, and evidence. It contains an
  orchestration layer and hosts harnesses as observed environments
  ([runtime primitive catalogs](03-architecture.md#runtime-primitive-catalogs)),
  but neither of those is what it is.
Not a prompt library, and not a wrapper that makes one vendor's model nicer.

Not a prescribed catalog of ideal agents, roles, personalities, workflows, or
  organizational doctrine. Bundled patterns are examples and optional starting
  points, not kernel truth.

Not dependent on a public marketplace. Local files, private catalogs,
  organization-internal registries, and offline or air-gapped installations
  remain complete authoring and distribution paths.

Not one prescribed autonomy curve. Presence and recorded time are policy
  inputs; an explicit owner policy may hold, shrink, grow, peak, reset, or loop
  scope and authority within its declared ceiling.

In the reference implementation, not a metrics theater: no invented numbers,
  no activity-as-progress, evidence precedes "done," and utilization is not the
  objective. A profile that omits verification says so instead.

The reference implementation is not finished when it works for its author:
  v1.0 means a person who has never read these docs can declare a bounded intent
  and receive a verifiable result.

orders.objective:
No gate fails late on bookkeeping, and no order pays the
complete gate more than once. Every `npm test` selection and `npm run
test:docs` begins with a structural phase: formatting, the configuration and
registration rows, the declaration scan over every suite's sources and every
copied-fixture closure, the freshness check of every generated artifact, and
the host's memory pressure. A structural failure stops the run before any
suite starts and names `npm run sync` when a generated artifact is stale;
`npm run sync` regenerates every derived artifact that policy allows and
names what it refuses and why. A failed task stops the run from starting
more unless `--keep-going` is given. `implementation-ready` and
`repair-complete` require the structural phase, the order's Preflight suites
and the document gate at the current code identity, not a complete run;
`final-review-result pass` requires one fresh complete `npm test -- --review
--again` row recorded in that review. The launchpad suite runs as file rows
under their own deadlines. A stopped run records what finished and answers
no claim.

The source writer cannot damage the operator's repository,
and a writer's request reaches the operator. The writer's owned command
route and profile are removed by two independent, absence-tolerant
removals; a failed removal is a typed cleanup outcome naming the surviving
path; admission and after-tests refuse while any grant survives; settlement,
`WorkerInterrupted` and integrity are recorded before the cleanup's result
is judged; a restart removes the survivors and admits. Before the focused
after-tests the worktree is judged against the committed tree (a
`skip-worktree` or `assume-unchanged` entry, or a byte or mode differing
from the committed blob, refuses naming the path; nothing is restored), and
the verification worktree reads Git under the host's writer-resistant
argument set, so hidden modified, deleted and executable-bit files never
reach after-testing or publication and a planted configuration, replace ref
or commit graph cannot change what verification judges. The writer commits
on a detached worktree into a private object store, reading the shared
store through a read-only alternate with no write access to the shared
`objects`, `refs` or `logs`; after admission the host imports the

orders.objective:
An instance controls the kit updates it takes, from core and
inside the instance:

- **Its own code.** `dotln.config.json` may declare `extensions`: a root
  outside every kit tree (default `extensions/`) and adapters by kind
  (`source`, `effect`, `projection`). A vertical issue naming
  `source: "<id>"` has `prepare()` load that adapter, record
  `ExtensionLoaded { id, kind, path, sha256 }` and call its `fetchBundle`
  in place of `fetchIssueBundle`, with the bundle passing the same checks
  as the GitHub source's; `effect` and `projection` adapters are admitted
  and listed, never imported here. No export, manifest or update touches
  the root; the README states the review burden. The first consumer is a
  fixture adapter; the enterprise-tracker adapter is the work instance's.
- **Its build.** The kit manifest names its build (the compiled definition
  modules, their semantic hash and compiler version). An update takes
  `both` (today's), `machinery` (build modules kept at their pinned bytes,
  `build.pin` recorded, emit, check and `kit-verify` honoring it) or `build`
  (the build alone, then the re-emit), and refuses an incompatible pairing
  before any write; inside an instance, the upgrade order runs
  `build --pin` or `build --take` after its merge, as the channel the
  operator chose. WO-076's overlay composes over whichever build is pinned.
- **Its way back.** Each update logs what it did and keeps retained copies,
  refusing before any write when it cannot. `rollback` inside the instance,
  or `export --update <dir> --rollback` from core, returns the kit files
  and manifest to the logged state before the last update, reverses the
  reversible instance actions (the update's `build.pin` among them), lists
  the rest by id, logs itself and prints the re-emit, which the role that
  ran it runs next; it refuses, naming the path or row, after a later kit
  edit, when the update is not the latest, or when a prior file has no
  verified source.
- **Its way in.** An instance takes a starter update only through an
  upgrade order that a planning pass (dedicated, or part of one) cuts from
  the kit's template. A planning branch writes only `docs/` and root
  Markdown (WO-135), so the pass never applies kit files. The order
  previews the update (WO-203), merges the named starter revision, runs the
  channel's `build` form, re-emits the build and passes the kit
  conformance tier; the template's rollback form takes the way back the
  same way.
- **Its gate (the planner's proposal, assumption 8).** Kit conformance:
  `kit-verify` on every gate, and the carried kit suites once per kit
  identity, a hash over the manifest-listed paths (and, while the overlay
  question stays open, the overlay file). The instance's own
  additions: suites it declares in `dotln.config.json` `suites` (name,
  command and sources), selected by changed sources, with each extension
  adapter naming the suite that covers it. Core's own gate is unchanged.
- **No step is the operator's by hand.** The operator gives the word (the
  starter revision, the channel, how each refused path resolves, a
  rollback), types the dispatch phrases and merges the pull request; a
  role runs every command and makes every commit (operator direction,
  2026-10-13; planning document §12.1).

## Goal-aligned decisions

The Contributor's purpose comes from [the vision](00-vision.md): DotLn is a
local-first, model-agnostic compiler/runtime for human judgment. This personal
implementation aims to improve operator flow by moving recurring supervision,
coordination, recovery and verification into dependable machinery, while
preserving correctness, authority, evidence, privacy and recoverability.

The current [critical-path plan](../planning/critical-path-2026-09-08.md) targets
the always-on runtime, its first real external source change and an independently
verified source-to-deliverable loop.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:start -->

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:end -->

**Platform lens.** Four checks from the platforms lesson the operator
pointed at (Steve Yegge's 2011 account of the Amazon service mandate) apply
to any capability a plan or order lands: it arrives as an interface
something else consumes (a transport profile, a typed event, a projection, a
handoff packet), never only as a script or a session; it is externalizable
by construction (content-addressed inputs, declared contracts, no private
setting as the source of a guarantee); this repository and the operator's
own repository consume it before any export; and its result is usable by a
stranger to the session, so a receipt that needs reverse-engineering is an
accessibility failure [[vision-into-use pass](../planning/vision-into-use-2026-09-17.md)
§12, 2026-09-17]. The planning refuter's platform-first standard is
unchanged.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:start -->

Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:end -->

The shared supports carry these duties and their compiled identity in both
harnesses. They are instruction-level judgment, not proof that an agent applied
every lens or a causal detector. The meter's five quantitative trap signals are
separate. General Naive Interventionism, NoOp and adaptive Tinkerer mechanics
retain their candidate scope; this bounded Contributor policy does not claim
their generalized implementations. The [WO-043 receipt](../evidence/WO-043/ideation-commands-and-usage.md)
records this promotion and its limits.

episode.statement: Plan refuter (identity Entropy Reducer, Contra-Auguste mask, architecture-and-semantics lens) for the 2026-10-17 standard pass at base a38a592e229a006f64e811231f7dc7e11472cb2c; model and effort not read back from the host. I read in full the canonical prompt docs/control/local/refute-2026-10-17.txt: its identity, work order, compiled subject (vision theses and exclusions, the five roles, the capability rows, the goal standard, the critical path, the five trap observations, the cost table and first verifications, the sixteen-order sequence, and the judged orders WO-216 to WO-220), output instructions, result schema and worker instructions. To check observations I read these, read-only: scripts/test-runner.mjs (suite table, --only selection, expandSuiteTasks, exclusive reservation, check row fields); scripts/lib/meta.mjs (gateStepCount and guardRefusals derivation); packages/skeleton/src/gate-evidence.mjs (readGateChecks, checksPath); the local gate index docs/control/local/harness/checks.json with its check-history, tallied for 2026-10-13T19:35Z to 2026-10-17T18:00Z by small node scripts in my session scratchpad that imported readGateChecks; scripts/lib/planning-followups.mjs (closed statuses, followupStatus, touchingFollowups); scripts/refute-plan.mjs (--touching defaults); scripts/host-guard.mjs (pressure sampling); scripts/release.mjs (check-surfaces); greps of scripts/check-publication.mjs, scripts/lib/evidence-sources.mjs, packages/skeleton/src/feedback-audit.ts and packages/skeleton/src/gate-deadlines.mjs; the test-case count of scripts/test-launchpad.mjs; git rev-parse; a names-only listing of the session scratch directory to check the output location (no planner scratch file opened); and existence checks of the files the five Cost lines name. The user and project instructions were supplied in context. I read no planning document, planning receipt, work-order file, follow-up register, intake, planner scratch file or earlier refutation. I ran no npm test or gate, used no model tools or subagents, and made no repository or Git write. Judgment: WO-216, WO-217, WO-218, WO-219 and WO-220 are each aligned-with-findings, the plan verdict is aligned-with-findings, and there are no hold reasons. Every finding is a known issue with a reopening observation, and none is an observed failure or vision contradiction. WO-216's NoOp cost (33 complete rows, median 1,689 s, 754 minutes, seven failed runs, none a product defect) reconciles with the gate index. The main issues: the structural phase now runs in front of every --only run (about 105 per order) and can block focused testing on a stale feedback edition; the launchpad file lanes drop an exclusive host reservation; and criterion 4 of each follow-up batch uses a textual pointer as a binding check, which conflicts with deferred rows, candidate rows and cross-batch files.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: no critical-path gate (A to P) names WO-216. It is UIFA devops machinery whose enabling claim is throughput for every later order, including gate P (WO-080, WO-083), which the sequence places after the five judged orders. The compiled order states its outcome (no late bookkeeping failure; one complete gate per order) but not the blocked product outcome the goal standard asks risk-reduction work to name. NoOp cost: I checked it against the local gate index (docs/control/local/harness/checks.json and check-history, read through readGateChecks) for 2026-10-13T19:35Z to 2026-10-17T18:00Z. There were 33 complete `npm test` rows (31 runs plus two companion rows), median 1,689 s, 754.0 minutes. Seven runs failed, matching the Cost line: process-debt at 27.1 min, format twice at 7 s, runner-fixtures at 41.3 min, wo107-schema at 38.1 min, and launchpad in the 44.7 and 18.5 min runs. There were 125 `test:docs` rows with 17 failures, 15 of them involving a generated artifact. Per closed order that is about 11 complete rows, mostly repeated passing full fresh runs, whether after identity changes or requested reruns is not distinguished here (WO-213 has 13 passing review rows, 9 of them with 91 or more fresh tasks). NoOp keeps paying about ten redundant complete runs per order and finds bookkeeping failures at minutes 5.6 to 22.2. The NoOp cost is observed. The saving is an inference that measured claim FUP-182984d482ca59ca is meant to test.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: the structural phase, the host precondition and refusals on four lifecycle claims are new refusal points. The policy-resistance signal counts hook denials only (meta.mjs guardRefusalCount over hook observations: 1, 1, 0, 25, 160), and bypassTools and adHocScripts are null, so WO-216's own refusals, and any bypass of the runner, stay invisible to the meter. Tragedy of the commons: fewer complete runs return host time, but launchpad file rows two at a time drop the current whole-host reservation of a suite that runs nested kit gates. Drift to low performance: it improves an explicit standard and records a baseline, but it changes the unit of gateStepCount (freshSuites plus reusedSuites of the last successful complete gate) just as the drift trap flags that series as worsening (91, 91, 97, 100, 103; reopenCandidate true). Escalation: it adds a script, a flag, refusals on four lifecycle claims, a role baseline in the chain and 15 criteria. It replaces separate regeneration commands with one sync, which works against escalation at handoff. But every `--only` run (314 single rows in the window, about 105 per order) gains the structural tasks. Success to the successful: it builds on the runner and gate-reuse; the smaller probe (make the existing preflight tasks stop the run on failure and change no claim) is not visible in the compiled subject. Shifting the burden: operatorCorrections is worsening (0, 1, 2, 5, 10; reopenCandidate true) and the order does not claim to reduce it; a warning-level host refusal hands memory relief to the operator. Rule beating: implementation-ready and verification-result pass on Preflight rows, WO-216 applies that rule to its own handoff, and the statistic "complete runs per closed order" counts 6 to 14 s reuse rows (8 of the 33) like 40-minute runs. Seeking the wrong goal: gate minutes are a means to operator flow. machineryShare is not worsening (0.16 for WO-213) and elapsedPerCodeByte rose to 304 for WO-213, so the target is a real cost rather than a proxy, provided the minutes statistic is the one that leads.
orders.removalBalance: Yes on the measured dimension, with one unnamed multiplier. Removal: about ten of eleven complete runs per order (754 minutes over three orders in the gate index; 545 gate task minutes per order on the Cost line), bookkeeping failures found in the first minute instead of at minutes 5.6 to 22.2, the document gate's duplicate copies of meta, index, release-surfaces, harness, the evidence checks and publication, and the separate regeneration commands. Addition: a structural phase of unknown duration (the coverage case alone ran about 19 s), `npm run sync` and scripts/test-sync.mjs, fail-fast with `--keep-going`, stopped-row recording, the finishedAt rule, claim changes for four lifecycle claims in resume, launchpad file rows, role text at about equal length, a new role baseline and fixtures. The unnamed multiplier: today `--only` selects only the named row (scripts/test-runner.mjs: `only ? row.name === only`), so the structural phase is added to about 105 single runs and 42 document runs per order. At 20 s that is about 50 minutes per order against several hours removed. Removal stays larger, but the Cost line should name the multiplier. The claim can be falsified through FUP-182984d482ca59ca.
orders.failureBehavior: Mixed. Some failures degrade to the old behavior: `--keep-going` restores run-everything; a passing complete row still satisfies implementation-ready, repair-complete and verification-result (criterion 10); a stopped run answers no claim and supplies no reuse; and sync refuses only what it may not mint and names the route. Others refuse instead of degrading. A structural failure stops every selection, including `--only` and the verifier's runs, and no keep-going route is named, so a false-stale artifact or a non-idempotent generator blocks all testing where the old runner still ran the suites. The host task refuses at warning, and the criteria do not say what it does when the pressure sample is unavailable, while the existing guard keeps its other signals and continues. final-review-result pass refuses without a fresh complete row with reusedSuites 0. That is the intended single complete run, but each failed final review then costs another fresh complete run.

findings.reason: Criterion 1 puts the six structural tasks in front of `--only` selections, which today run only the named row. Criterion 3 fails `generated` on any stale evidence edition, and criterion 6 has sync refuse a feedback edition whose judged sources changed. Inference: while an order edits a judged source, every focused run refuses until a live feedback episode re-mints the edition, and each further edit makes it stale again. The cheapest workaround, running suite files directly with node --test, is unobserved because bypassTools and adHocScripts are null. WO-217 to WO-220 expect to edit judged sources.

findings.reason: The Cost line gives the structural phase's duration as unknown per run but omits how many runs pay it. In the window, 314 single (`--only`) rows and 125 document rows were recorded across three orders, about 147 per order. All of them gain the structural phase, and the measured claim's three statistics do not count this added time.

findings.reason: The host precondition refuses at warning as well as critical, and criterion 4 says nothing about an unavailable sample, for example on a host or sandbox without the macOS pressure signal. The existing guard degrades: it reports "signal unavailable; keeping other signals" and continues. A refusal at warning hands memory relief to the operator during the multi-session work that produces the pressure.

findings.reason: Launchpad file rows "two at a time" conflict with the suite's current reservation. Today the launchpad row is `exclusive: true`, with the comment "Its nested kit gates inherit this reservation rather than one lane", and reservedSlots gives an exclusive row every slot. Two concurrent file rows each run nested kit gates, which raises the host memory pressure that caused one of the seven failures. The host check runs only before the run starts.

findings.reason: Handoff and verification now pass on structural, Preflight and document rows, so a product defect in a suite outside the Preflight line surfaces only at final review, after verification has passed. The evidence that this is safe is three orders: seven failed complete runs and no product defect, which the gate index confirms. First verifications failed in 5 of the last 8 orders, so repair loops are common. WO-216 also applies the new claim rule to its own handoff (criterion 13).

findings.reason: The measured claim may not isolate WO-216's effect. It is read over "the five closes after this order's", which by the sequence are WO-217 to WO-220 and WO-080. Those batches each add fail-first fixture cases, which grow the suites. In addition, "complete runs per closed order (baseline 11)" counts reuse rows of 6 to 14 s, 8 of the 33 in the gate index, the same as 40-minute runs. The count can fall and gate task minutes can rise from suite growth, so neither statistic alone shows the effect.

findings.reason: WO-216 changes the granularity of the unit the drift trap counts. gateStepCount is freshSuites plus reusedSuites of the latest successful complete gate. Folding the existing meta, harness and evidence preflight tasks into one generated task would lower it (inference), and per-file launchpad rows raise it, while the trap flags that series as worsening (91, 91, 97, 100, 103; reopenCandidate true). The Cost line names no re-baseline, so the next reading reflects the unit change rather than a trend.

findings.reason: The structural, host and claim refusals are runner and resume refusals, and the policy-resistance signal counts only hook denials. So the meter cannot see whether WO-216's own refusals provoke workarounds, which is the trap the order is most exposed to.

A false stale reading would therefore block all testing, including the verifier's `--only` runs, where the old runner still ran the suites.

The substance holds: 15 of 17 failures involved a generated artifact. Under the platform lens, a receipt that needs reverse-engineering is an accessibility cost.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: none is named. Its surfaces (runner, gate-reuse, host guard, machinery coverage, observed facts, gate evidence, product read guard) are UIFA devops machinery shared by every gate, and they are the subsystem WO-216 restructures. It serves throughput, not a specific product gate. The 31 row ids are not in the compiled subject, so which rows block which order cannot be judged here. NoOp cost in the records, the Cost line being the only record supplied: each of the 31 rows was still pending at 7b8206f4; the "next order that edits the surface" rule delivered none of them; and the register holds 281 pending rows (130 decision rows, 151 candidates; 88 boarded from 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-17). The harm each row causes now is "unknown until each row is triaged". NoOp therefore means the backlog persists with unknown per-row harm: not shown to be zero, not shown to be material. The five judged orders precede WO-080, WO-204 (source-writer containment), WO-192 and WO-083, and the NoOp of delaying those by one order is not recorded.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: criterion 4 turns a self-declared pointer (followups --touching) into a verdict, and deferred is not a closed status, so criteria 1 and 4 can undo one another. Tragedy of the commons: an edited judged source owes a live feedback episode on a max or xhigh model, "cost accepted" with tokens unknown, and after WO-216 every focused run refuses while that edition is stale, so more than one episode per order is plausible. Drift to low performance: the measured outcome is a register count; each settled row needs a fixture that fails without the fix, which keeps it above activity-as-progress, but no outcome standard is named. Escalation: each settled row adds a fixture case to suites WO-216 is trying to make cheaper (at most one third declined, so at least about 21 fixes or already-met commands). Success to the successful: the batch template is preferred to repairing the routing rule the Cost line shows delivered none of these rows; that alternative is not visible in the subject. Shifting the burden: planning-cut cleanup batches are the intervenor while the inflow (88 rows in five days over three closes) continues, and operator-only rows leave as packets while operatorCorrections is worsening (0, 1, 2, 5, 10). Rule beating: "settled" admits a row the current source already meets with a command and its output, and the decline cap is a quota. Seeking the wrong goal: the order advances operator flow only if its rows are defects that cost supervision; per-row harm is unknown until triage. Specific to WO-217: it edits scripts/test-runner.mjs and scripts/lib/gate-reuse.mjs, which WO-216 rewrites, and the compiled subject declares no dependency between the two orders, so rows can be overtaken by WO-216 or fixed twice.
orders.removalBalance: Not shown; unknown, not a structural hold. The named removal is 31 pending register rows, a record count. The named addition is the fixes and fail-first fixture cases across eight named files plus fixtures, 15 steps, any live feedback episodes, re-mints and a complete review gate, every one "unknown until each row is triaged". The two are not commensurable and the harm each row causes now is not stated, so the Cost line does not name a removal larger than its addition. It is also gross, not net: the order's own verification and review will board rows at a rate the subject puts near 29 per close. The settled rows' fixtures are a permanent addition to gate time.
orders.failureBehavior: Partly refuses. A fix whose fixture fails fails the gate as before, and a row that cannot be fixed may be declined with harm, evidence and a reversal condition, which degrades to the old state of a pending row with a reason. But WO-217 cannot complete when more than one third of its rows merit declining (criterion 3), or when criterion 4's textual match lists a deferred row, a candidate row or another batch's row. Those cases refuse completion rather than degrade, and the only release is an operator decision. Nothing in the order lets a row fall back to "pending, routed to the next order that edits the surface", the old behavior.

findings.reason: Criterion 4 makes `npm run plan -- followups --touching` a binding completion check, but the command declares itself "a pointer for judgment and never a verdict" and its matching cannot separate this order's obligations from others. Checked in code: `deferred` is not a closed status (closed = allocated, declined, duplicate, settled), touchingFollowups keeps every entry whose status is not closed with no kind filter, and with no terms the CLI matches the worktree's changed paths and the worktree's own order id. So (a) a row WO-217 defers under criterion 1, whose disposition names its packet in docs/evidence/WO-217/handoff.md or WO-217, stays pending and is listed, failing criterion 4; (b) a candidate row (151 at the base, left to planning by the non-goals) that names a changed file's path or base name is listed; (c) a row of another batch naming a shared file is listed although the non-goals exclude other batches. Constructible, not observed: it needs one such row.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-217's `followups --touching` lists a row WO-217 deferred under criterion 1, a candidate row, or a row allocated to another batch.

findings.reason: The title says the 31 rows are "listed below" and criterion 1 says "every row id listed above", but the compiled subject carries no row ids. Which critical-path gate each row unblocks, and the NoOp harm of each, cannot be judged from the subject this refutation was given; the order also names no blocked outcome, which the goal standard asks risk-reduction work to name.
findings.reopenWhen: The compiled subject carries WO-217's row ids, or a listed row is shown to block WO-080, WO-204, WO-192 or WO-083.

findings.reason: The objective treats the stock, not the inflow. By the Cost line's own figures, 88 pending follow-ups were boarded from 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-17 (its "88 of them" does not say whether of the 281 or of the 130) while three orders closed (inference: about 29 per close). The four batches take 123 rows; at that rate the five closes WO-216 to WO-220 would board about as many again, and the "next order that edits the surface" rule the Cost line shows delivered none of these 31 rows stays the general rule (criterion 4 applies it to this order only). The register count is a proxy; the outcome it stands for (defects that cost supervision) is unmeasured per row.
